title: Smoky Barbecue Haloumi Sandwich
subtitle: with Pickles and Sweet Potato Chips
description: Whether you're full-time vego or part-time only, our varied range of vegetarian dishes really hits the spot. Bursting with veggies, dairy, legumes, grains and nuts, they're packed with flavour, they’ll fill you up and they're totally mouth-watering too!

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Preheat the oven to 220C, fan-forced. Line an oven tray with baking paper. Cut the unpeeled sweet potato into 1cm-thick chips. Thinly slice the cucumber and onion. Slice the haloumi.

Roast sweet potato: Put the sweet potato, 1 tbs olive oil and 1 tsp barbecue seasoning in a bowl, season with salt and pepper and toss to coat. Put on the lined tray and roast for 20 mins or until tender. Reserve the bowl.

Pickle cucumber: Meanwhile, put 1 tbs white vinegar and 1 tsp sugar in a large bowl, season with salt and stir until the sugar dissolves. Add the cucumber and toss to coat. Set aside to pickle. Put the haloumi in the reserved bowl. Add the remaining barbecue seasoning and 1 tbs olive oil and stir to combine.

Cook haloumi and onion: Heat a medium frypan over medium-high heat. Cook the haloumi for 2 mins each side or until golden. Remove from the pan. Cook the onion, stirring, for 3 mins or until the onion is softened. Remove the pan from the heat. Cut the bread rolls in half. Put on an oven tray, cut side up, and bake for 5 mins or until lightly toasted.

Serve up: Spread the bread roll bases and tops with the mayonnaise. Layer the bases with the haloumi, onion and drained pickled cucumber, then sandwich with the tops. Serve with the sweet potato chips and enjoy!

Did you know?: Haloumi is a brined, slightly springy cheese originally from Cyprus. Traditionally it was made from a mixture of goat and sheep milk, although these days cow's milk is also used. The haloumi we use is made using vegetable rennet, so it's suitable for vegetarians.
